vulnerable_statements.reason: The XDP program setup changes vsi->xdp_prog, XDP rings and queue vectors without holding any lock that serializes against the VSI reset/rebuild path. The rebuild path rebuilds the same rings and q_vectors under a different lock, so a concurrent reset and XDP reconfiguration can race and corrupt ring state. That can cause a NULL dereference or use-after-free.

Setting up the AF_XDP pool (stopping and restarting a queue pair and swapping the pool) has the same problem: it is not synchronized with the reset/rebuild path, so it can work on rings that are being freed or reallocated.

suggested_fix: Add a per-VSI mutex (e.g. vsi->xdp_state_lock) and hold it around the whole XDP_SETUP_PROG and XDP_SETUP_XSK_POOL switch in ice_xdp(). Take the same mutex in the VSI rebuild/reset path, where XDP rings and q_vectors are rebuilt. Inside the lock, also check whether a reset is in progress (e.g. ice_is_reset_in_progress) and return -EBUSY if so. Move all the returns into a single unlock-and-return path.
